3120.h: 277 - Abū al-Walīd al-Faqīh Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad *
3120.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the unique, the hadith master (الحافظ), the mufti (المفتي), the shaykh of Khurasan, Abū al-Walīd Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Hārūn al-Naysābūrī, al-Shāfiʿī, the devout worshipper (العابد). ⟦15:492⟧
He was born: after the year 270.
He heard from: أبي عبد الله محمد بن إبراهيم البوشنجي، وابن خزيمة، وعدة ببلده، والحسن بن سفيان بنسا، وأحمد بن الحسن بن عبد الجبار الصوفي ببغداد، وهذه الطبقة.
He studied jurisprudence under Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn Surayj, who was the holder of a view within the school.
Among the strangest things he came up with is that he said: Whoever repeats al-Fātiḥah twice, his prayer is invalid; and this contradicts the explicit text of the Imam (الإمام).
And he said: Cupping breaks the fast of the one who cups and the one who is cupped, and he held firmly that this is the position of the school because the hadiths on it are authentic (الصحيح).
This is open to question, because the Imam (الإمام) (1) did not declare the hadiths weak (ضعيف), but rather claimed that they were abrogated (2) . ⟦15:493⟧
Narrating from him: الحاكم، وابن مندة، وأبو طاهر بن محمش، والقاضي أحمد بن الحسن الحيري، وأبو الفضل أحمد بن محمد السهلي الصفار، وعدة.
al-Ḥākim said: Abū al-Walīd compiled (al-Mustakhraj ʿalā Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim)
and compiled (al-Aḥkām) according to the school of al-Shāfiʿī (1) .
Abū Saʿd the man of letters (الأديب) said: I asked Abū ʿAlī al-Thaqafī, and said: Whom shall we ask after you?
He said: Abū al-Walīd (2) .
al-Ḥākim said: I heard the master Abū al-Walīd say: My father said to me: What are you collecting?
I said: I am extracting on (Kitāb al-Bukhārī) .
So he said: You should take (Kitāb Muslim) , for it is more blessed, since al-Bukhārī was ascribed to the position on the wording (3) .
Muḥammad ibn al-Dhuhlī said: And Muslim too was ascribed to the wording; do you not see how he got up from the session of al-Dhuhlī in front of the assembly when he said: Whoever says the saying of Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, let him not come near us?
This is a problematic issue, and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and others did not consider it right to delve into this issue, although al-Bukhārī - (may Allah have mercy on him) - did not state that explicitly, nor did he say: Our utterances of the Qurʾān are created.
Rather he said: Our acts are created, while what is recited and uttered is the speech of Allah - (Exalted is He) -, and is not created; so silence about the broadening of expressions is safer for a person. ⟦15:494⟧
This Abū al-Walīd was indeed one of the pillars of the religion.
When he died, Abū Ṭāhir ibn Maḥmish the jurist (الفقيه) - one of his students - eulogised him with a poem of sixty verses (1) .
al-Ḥākim said: Abū al-Walīd showed us the engraving on his seal: Allah is the reliance of Ḥassān ibn Muḥammad.
And he said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAdī showed us the engraving on his seal: Allah is the reliance of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muḥammad.
And he said: al-Rabīʿ showed us the engraving on his seal: Allah is the reliance of al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān.
And he said: The engraving on the seal of al-Shāfiʿī was: Allah is the reliance of Muḥammad ibn Idrīs (2) .
This is an established chain of transmission (الإسناد).
Abū al-Walīd died: in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal, in the year 349 AH, aged 72.
al-Ḥākim said: He is Abū al-Walīd al-Qurashī al-Umawī al-Shāfiʿī, the Imam (الإمام) of the people of hadith in Khurasan, and the most ascetic (الزاهد) of the scholars I have seen and the most devout worshipper (العابد) among them; he studied jurisprudence in Baghdad under Ibn Surayj (3) .
I say: Dying in the same year were: the scholar of Isfahan, the judge (القاضي) Abū Aḥmad al-ʿAssāl; the hadith master (الحافظ) of Khurasan Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Zayd al-Naysābūrī; the musnid (المسند) of the age in Egypt Abū al-Fawāris Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Sindī al-Ṣābūnī; the musnid (المسند) of Baghdad Aḥmad ibn ʿUthmān ibn Yaḥyā al-Adamī al-ʿAṭshī; Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Khurāsānī; the musnid (المسند) of Damascus Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ṣāliḥ Sinān al-Makhzūmī; the shaykh of the reciters (القارئ) Abū Ṭāhir ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Abī Hāshim; the long-lived ⟦15:495⟧ Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmrawayh ibn ʿIlm al-Ṣaffār; and Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq ibn Nīkhāb al-Ṭayyibī in Baghdad.
أخبرنا أحمد بن هبة الله، أنبأنا القاسم بن عبد الله الصفار، أخبرتنا عائشة بنت أحمد، أخبرنا الحسن بن علي البستي، أخبرنا يحيى بن إبراهيم المزكي، حدثنا الزاهد إمام عصره أبو الوليد حسان بن محمد الفقيه، حدثنا أبو عبد الله البوشنجي، حدثنا يحيى بن بكير، حدثني الليث، عن ابن الهاد، عن ابن شهاب، عن عروة، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate in his prayer: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the False Messiah, the Antichrist, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of life and death. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and from debt” (1) The hadith continues.

1132.h: 133 - Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Hamdānī * (ع)
1132.t:
The hadith master (الحافظ), the Imam (الإمام), the authority (الحجة), Abū Yūsuf al-Hamdānī, al-Sabīʿī, al-Kūfī.
He narrated extensively from: his grandfather.
He also narrated from: زياد بن علاقة، وآدم بن علي، وآدم بن سليمان أبي يحيى، وإسماعيل السدي، وعاصم بن بهدلة، وعبد الكريم الجزري، وإبراهيم بن عبد الأعلى، وعبد الأعلى بن عامر الثعلبي، وأشعث بن أبي الشعثاء، وثوير بن أبي فاختة، وسعد أبي مجاهد الطائي، وسعيد بن مسروق، وسماك بن حرب، وعامر بن شقيق بن جمرة الأسدي، وعبد العزيز بن رفيع، وعثمان بن عاصم، ومخارق الأحمسي، ومنصور بن المعتمر، وخلق كثير. ⟦7:355⟧
He was one of the vessels of hadith, and one of those called Shaykh al-Islām (شيخ الإسلام), like his father, his grandfather, and his brother ʿĪsā.
Narrating from him: أخوه، وحجاج الأعور، وأحمد بن خالد الوهبي، وآدم بن أبي إياس، وعبد الرزاق، ومحمد بن سابق، وشبابة، وإسحاق بن منصور السلولي، وأحمد بن يونس، وحسين بن محمد المروذي، وعبد الله بن رجاء، وأبو نعيم، ومحمد بن كثير العبدي، وأبو غسان النهدي، ومحمد بن يوسف الفريابي، وأبو سلمة التبوذكي، ويحيى بن أبي كثير، ووكيع، ويحيى بن آدم، وعلي بن الجعد، ومعاوية بن عمرو الأزدي، وأبو الوليد الطيالسي، وخلق كثير.
He narrated: هارون بن حاتم، عن دبيس بن حميد: that Isrāʾīl was born in the year 100.
He narrated: عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، عن عيسى بن يونس، قال:
Isrāʾīl said to me: I used to memorise the hadith of Abū Isḥāq as I memorise a sūrah of the Qurʾān.
Ibn al-Madīnī, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, said: Isrāʾīl is above Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh.
Ḥarb al-Kirmānī narrated from Aḥmad, who said: He was reliable (ثقة), and he kept expressing wonder at his memory.
As for Ṣāliḥ ibn Aḥmad, he narrated from his father, who said: Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq: he is soft in hadith (لين الحديث); he heard from him late.
Abū Ṭālib said: Aḥmad was asked: Who is more firmly reliable (ثبت): Sharīk or Isrāʾīl?
He said: Isrāʾīl used to relay what he heard; he was more firmly reliable (ثبت) than Sharīk.
I said: Whom do you prefer: Yūnus, or Isrāʾīl his son, regarding Abū Isḥāq?
He said: Isrāʾīl, because he had a book.
al-Faḍl ibn Ziyād said: I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh: Whom do you prefer: Yūnus or Isrāʾīl regarding Abū Isḥāq?
He said: Yūnus. ⟦7:356⟧
Abū Dāwūd said: I said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal (1) : When Isrāʾīl is alone in narrating a hadith, is he used as proof (يحتج به)?
He said: Isrāʾīl is firmly reliable (ثبت) in hadith; Yaḥyā used to lay blame on him in the matter of Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt.
He said: He narrated rejected (المنكر) reports from him (2) .
Then Aḥmad said: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated nothing from him.
Aḥmad said: And Isrāʾīl, when he narrates from his book, leaves nothing out, and he memorises from his book.
And in one narration, from Aḥmad, he said: Sharīk is more precise than Isrāʾīl regarding Abū Isḥāq.
ʿAbbās narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said: al-Qaṭṭān did not narrate from Isrāʾīl, nor from Sharīk.
Ibn Maʿīn said: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam said: We used to write at Isrāʾīl’s from his memory.
Yaḥyā said: Isrāʾīl did not memorise, then he memorised afterwards - meaning: that he studied his book -.
And Yaḥyā said: Isrāʾīl is more firmly reliable (ثبت) regarding Abū Isḥāq than Shaybān.
Aḥmad ibn Zuhayr and others narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn: reliable (ثقة).
And al-ʿIjlī said: reliable (ثقة).
And Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī said: reliable (ثقة), truthful (صدوق), among the most precise of the companions of Abū Isḥāq.
And Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah said: truthful (صدوق), but not strong.
And he said once: he is soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd al-Ḥaddānī said: I heard ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus say:
Our companions were Sufyān and Sharīk ... and he counted some people who, when they disagreed about the hadith of Abū Isḥāq, would come to my father, and he would say: Go to my son Isrāʾīl, for he narrates it more than I do, ⟦7:357⟧
and is more precise in it than I am, and he was the guide of his grandfather.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Thalj narrated from Shabābah:
I said to Yūnus: Dictate to me the hadith of your father.
He said: Write from Isrāʾīl, for my father dictated it to him.
al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Jarjarāʾī, from Khalaf ibn Tamīm: I heard Abū al-Aḥwaṣ - if Allah wills - mention from Abū Isḥāq, who said:
Isrāʾīl left us no window and no basket without stuffing it (1) with books.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥunaynī: I heard Abū Nuʿaym being asked: Who is more firmly reliable (ثبت): Isrāʾīl or Abū ʿAwānah?
He said: Isrāʾīl.
And al-Nasāʾī said: no harm in him (لا بأس به).
I say: The majority praised Isrāʾīl, and he was used as proof (يحتج به) by the two Shaykhs, and he was a hadith master (الحافظ), a man of a book and of knowledge.
Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Barāʾ narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī: Isrāʾīl is weak (ضعيف).
I say: ʿAlī followed his teacher Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, and Abū Muḥammad ibn Ḥazm followed in their footsteps, and said: weak (ضعيف).
And he set out to deal with his hadiths that are in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين), and rejected them, and considered them not used as proof (يحتج به); so pay no attention to that, for he is reliable (ثقة).
Yes, he is not, in verification, like Sufyān and Shuʿbah, though perhaps he comes close to them in the hadith of his grandfather, for he accompanied him morning and evening for ten years, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to narrate from him and strengthen him, and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd achieved nothing by abandoning narration from him while narrating from Mujālid (2) . ⟦7:358⟧
ʿAbbās narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, who said:
Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah, Zuhayr, and Isrāʾīl: their hadith from Abū Isḥāq is close to equal; the true companions of Abū Isḥāq are Sufyān and Shuʿbah.
ʿAbbās al-Dūrī said: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying:
Isrāʾīl came to Baghdad and the people gathered around him, and he was seated on a raised place; a man with a notebook stood and began to ask him from it, while the people could not look into it; and when Isrāʾīl got up, that man sat down and dictated it to the people (1) .
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī used to say: Isrāʾīl is more firmly reliable (ثبت) regarding Abū Isḥāq than Shuʿbah and al-Thawrī.
I say: I lean toward this more than toward what came before, for Isrāʾīl was the crutch of his grandfather, and alongside his knowledge and memory he was a man of righteousness and humility - (may Allah have mercy on him) - and his brother ʿĪsā was more precise than he, more knowledgeable, and a greater devout worshipper (العابد) - (may Allah be pleased with both of them) -.
Abū Aḥmad ibn ʿAdī made the biography long (2) , and listed for him a number of gharīb (الغريب) hadiths.
It has reached us from Shaqīq al-Balkhī, who said:
I learned humility from Isrāʾīl; we would be around him and he would not know who was on his right nor who was on his left, because of his reflection on the Hereafter; so I knew that he was a righteous man.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said: Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān said: Isrāʾīl is above Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh.
Yaḥyā was told: Isrāʾīl narrated 300 hadiths from Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir and 300 from Abū Yaḥyā al-Qattāt?
He said: The fault is not from him; the fault came from the two of them together (3) . ⟦7:359⟧
I say: He alludes to Ibn Muhājir and al-Qattāt being soft in hadith (لين الحديث).
And among Isrāʾīl’s gharīb (الغريب) reports: Aḥmad narrated in his (Musnad) : حدثنا أبو سعيد، حدثنا إسرائيل، حدثنا سعيد بن مسروق، عن سعد بن عبيدة، عن ابن عمر:
from ʿUmar that he said: No, by my father!
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Stop! Whoever swears by anything other than Allah has associated partners with Allah (1)” .
Its narrators are reliable (ثقة).
And among his elevated chains (العالي): أنبأنا عبد الرحمن بن قدامة الفقيه، أنبأنا عمر بن محمد، أنبأنا هبة الله بن محمد، أنبأنا محمد بن محمد بن غيلان، حدثنا أبو بكر الشافعي، حدثنا إبراهيم بن عبد الرحيم بن دنوقا، حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح العجلي، حدثنا إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite: “Indeed, it is I who am the Provider, the Possessor of Strength, the Firm (2)” (Qurʾān 51:58).
And this is a gharīb (الغريب) hadith.
Abū Nuʿaym al-Mulāʾī and Qaʿnab ibn al-Muḥarrar said: Isrāʾīl died in the year 160 AH.
And Ibn Saʿd and Shabāb (3) al-ʿUṣfurī said: He died in the year 162 AH. ⟦7:360⟧
And Muṭayyan said: He died in the year 1.

4116.h: 40 - al-Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā al-Baghdādī Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn *
4116.t:
The Imam (الإمام), the great scholar, the shaykh of the Ḥanbalīs, the judge (القاضي), Abū Yaʿlā Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Khalaf ibn Aḥmad al-Baghdādī, al-Ḥanbalī, Ibn al-Farrāʾ, author of the great (al-Taʿlīqah) and of useful works on the school.
He was born: at the beginning of the year 380.
He heard from: علي بن عمر الحربي، وإسماعيل بن سويد، وأبا القاسم بن حبابة، وعيسى بن الوزير، وابن أخي ميمي، وأم الفتح بنت أحمد بن كامل، وأبا طاهر المخلص، وأبا الطيب بن منتاب، وابن معروف القاضي، وطائفة.
And he dictated a number of sessions.
Narrating from him: الخطيب، وأبو الخطاب الكلوذاني، وأبو الوفاء بن عقيل، وأبو غالب بن البناء، وأخوه يحيى بن البناء، وأبو العز بن كادش، وأبو بكر محمد بن عبد الباقي، وابنه القاضي أبو الحسين محمد بن محمد ⟦18:89⟧ بن الفراء، وأبو سعد أحمد بن محمد الزوزني.
Among the earlier ones, the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ) Abū ʿAlī al-Ahwāzī also narrated from him.
He issued legal opinions and taught, his companions graduated under him, and leadership in jurisprudence (الفقه) came to rest with him, and he was the scholar of Iraq in his time, with knowledge of the sciences of the Qurʾān and its exegesis (التفسير), and of debate and the principles; his father was among the notables of the Ḥanafīs and among the witnesses of the Court, and he died when Abū Yaʿlā was ten years old, so his Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ) taught him the acts of worship from the (Mukhtaṣar) of al-Khiraqī, and jurisprudence (الفقه) became sweet to him, and he moved to the circle of Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid (1) , the shaykh of the Ḥanbalīs, and accompanied him for years, and excelled in jurisprudence (الفقه) under him, and by his command took the seat for teaching in the year 402, and the beginning of his direct hearing (السماع) from ʿAlī ibn Maʿrūf was in the year (385) .
He also heard in Mecca and Damascus from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Naṣr, and in Aleppo, and he compiled the book (Ibṭāl Taʾwīl al-Ṣifāt) and they rose against him because of the flimsy and fabricated (الموضوع) material in it; so the creed that he had compiled went out to the scholars from al-Qādir bi-llāh, and the book (Ibṭāl al-Taʾwīl) was carried to al-Qādir and pleased him, and matters and trials occurred - we ask Allah for well-being - then the vizier ʿAlī ibn al-Muslimah reconciled the two parties, and said before the assembly: The Qurʾān is the speech of Allah, and the reports of the attributes are passed on as they came (2) .
Then Abū Yaʿlā assumed the judgeship of the Abode of the Caliphate and the Ḥarīm, together with the judgeship of Ḥarrān (3) and Ḥulwān (4) , and he had recited the ten recitation traditions (القراءات), and he was a man of worship and night prayer, and of constant devotion ⟦18:90⟧ to authorship, with grandeur and awe, but he had no strong hand in the knowledge of hadith, so at times he argued from flimsy reports.
Studying jurisprudence under him: أبو الحسن البغدادي، وأبو جعفر الهاشمي، وأبو الغنائم بن الغباري، وأبو علي بن البناء، وأبو الوفاء بن القواس، وأبو الحسن النهري، وابن عقيل، وأبو الخطاب، وأبو الحسن بن جدا، وأبو يعلى الكيال، وأبو الفرج الشيرازي.
He wrote the book (Aḥkām al-Qurʾān) , and (Masāʾil al-Īmān) , and (al-Muʿtamad) and its abridgement, and (al-Muqtabas) , and (ʿUyūn al-Masāʾil) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Karrāmiyyah) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Sālimiyyah wa-al-Mujassimah) , and (al-Radd ʿalā al-Jahmiyyah) , and (al-Kalām fī al-Istiwāʾ) , and (al-ʿUddah) on the principles of jurisprudence (1) ; and its abridgement, and (Faḍāʾil Aḥmad) , and the book (al-Ṭibb) , and many other works that I listed in (Tārīkh al-Islām (2)) .
He was self-restrained, pure of soul, of great standing, deeply scrupulous.
He died: in the year 458 AH.
And dying in the same year were: al-Bayhaqī (3) , the judge (القاضي) of Sāriyah Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Sarawī (4) , Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Ghālib the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ), Abū al-Ṭayyib ʿAbd al-Razzāq ibn Shamah (5) , and Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Sīdah (6) - author of ⟦18:91⟧ (al-Muḥkam) - and the judge (القاضي) Abū ʿĀṣim Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-ʿAbbādī in Herat (1) .

2327.h: 115 - Ibn Bulbul al-Shaybānī Abū al-Ṣaqr Ismāʿīl **
2327.t:
The great vizier, the unique, the man of letters (الأديب), Abū al-Ṣaqr Ismāʿīl ibn Bulbul al-Shaybānī. ⟦13:199⟧
One of the poets, the eloquent, and the generous who were praised.
He served as vizier to al-Muʿtamid in the year 265 AH, after al-Ḥasan ibn Makhlad (1) , then was dismissed, then served as vizier again, then was dismissed, then served as vizier a third time upon the arrest of the vizier Ṣāʿid, in the year 72.
He was at the rank of the great kings, with a great stipend: every day a hundred sheep, seventy kids, and a hundredweight of sweets; and when al-Muʿtaḍid became crown prince, he arrested him and tortured him until he perished in the year 278 AH.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭāhir said: al-Muwaffaq’s choice for his vizierate fell upon Abū al-Ṣaqr, so he took as vizier a man whose like was seldom seen: competent for the important matter, independent in affairs, the most effective in planning along its soundest paths and those of greatest benefit, the most protective of the affairs of the sultan, along with raising the standing of literary learning and its people, and his giving them precious things, along with courage, high aspiration, and the world being small in his eyes except what he put forward for his return to Allah, along with breadth of forbearance and restraint of anger, and generosity to the one who had wished his destruction.
Abū ʿAlī al-Tanūkhī said: حدثنا أبو الحسين عبد الله بن أحمد، حدثنا سليمان بن الحسن قال:
Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Furāt said: I attended the session of Ibn Bulbul, when he held a general sitting, and the petitioners entered upon him, and he looked into their affairs, and no one left except with a gift, or an appointment, or the fulfilment of a need, or redress; and one man remained at the end of the session asking him to release the lease of his village.
He said: al-Muwaffaq commanded that I release nothing except by his order, so I will inform him.
He said: The man spoke to us again, and said: If the vizier delays me, my situation will be ruined.
So he said to his scribe: Write his need in the memorandum.
The man turned away, not far ⟦13:200⟧ off, then returned and asked permission, then said:
Not in every dynasty and every hour ... are acts of kindness made ready
So if one day the age gives you the chance ... then hasten to them before the vicissitudes of time
He said to me: O Abū al-ʿAbbās, write for him the release of the lease of his estate right now.
And he ordered the money-changer to pay him 500 dinars.
It is said: His servant handed him ink with the pen, and it dripped onto a costly cloak, and he was alarmed; so he said: Do not be alarmed, then recited:
If musk perfumes the scent of some people ... the fragrance of ink suffices me for that
For nothing is finer than garments ... on whose edges is the blackness of soot
I say: He spoke truly, and it is a beauty mark on the clothing of viziers.
Jaḥẓah (1) said: I said:
Through Abū al-Ṣaqr, upon us ... are the glorious blessings of Allah
A king in whose eyes this world ... is little for the one who hopes in him
So he ordered for me 200 dinars.
al-Ṣūlī said: Ibn Bulbul was born in the year 230 AH, and I saw him several times; he was at the utmost of beauty and complete in stature and body; he was arrested in Ṣafar, in the year 278, and fettered, and made to wear a cloak dipped in molasses and trotter broth, and seated in ⟦13:201⟧ a hot place, and tortured with all kinds of torture, and he died in Jumādā al-Ūlā.
And it is said: He was seen in a dream and it was said to him: What did Allah do with you?
He said: He forgave me because of what I met with; He would not have combined for me the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.
Abū ʿAlī al-Tanūkhī narrated from his father, from a group of the people of the court, who informed him:
that al-Muʿtaḍid gave an order concerning Ibn Bulbul, and a large trough (1) was made for him, and it was filled with white lead and water, then his head was put into it up to his neck, and he was held down until he was extinguished, and his soul kept coming out through flatulence from below until he died.
